text:
Goikhberg c. Mankovitz

2016 QCCQ 11250

COURT OF QUEBEC

Small Claims Division

CANADA

PROVINCE OF QUÉBEC

DISTRICT OF

MONTRÉAL

Civil Division

No:

500-32-150301-150

DATE:

Octobre 19
th
,
2016

______________________________________________________________________

BEFORE
THE HONOURABLE MARTINE L. TREMBLAY, J.C.Q.

______________________________________________________________________

YAFIM
GOIKHBERG

Plaintiff

v.

Deborah mankoviTZ

Defendant

______________________________________________________________________

JUDGMENT

______________________________________________________________________

[
1
]

Mr. Yafim Goikhberg (“
Mr. Goikhberg
”)
claims that in November 2014, Me Deborah Mankovitz (“
Me Mankovitz
”)
verbally agreed to pay him $ 15,000 in compensation for the damages resulting
from the false information that she gave to various authorities and that led to
his indictment for violation of the
Immigration and Refugee Protection Act
(the
“
IRPA
”)
[1]

on September 26, 2011
[2]
.

[
2
]

Me Mankovitz denies the existence of such an
agreement. She pleads that Mr. Goikhberg is alleging that the false statements
were made in 2009. Therefore, the action that was instituted on December 14,
2015 is prescribed. She adds that, in any event, a lawyer may not be subject to
suits by third parties for facts alleged in Court proceedings or other
documents prepared on behalf of a client. Finally, she argues that Mr.
Goikhberg is a vexatious litigant and the suit is abusive.

ISSUES

1)

Is there an agreement between Mr.
Goikhberg and Me Mankovitz for the payment of $ 15,000?

2)

Can Me Mankovitz be condemned to pay
damages to Mr. Goikhberg for the statements made on behalf of Ms. Dakhova to
the Board and the Federal Court?

3)

Is Mr. Goikhberg’s action abusive,
frivolous or does it reflects a conduct that is vexatious or quarrelsome?

FACTS

[
3
]

From the evidence adduced at trial, the Court
summarized hereafter only the relevant facts.

[
4
]

Ms. Natalia Dakhova (“
Ms. Dakhova
”)
arrived from Kirghizstan in May 2006.
[3]

On January 18, 2007 she filed an application claiming refugee status in Canada
for fear of being
“killed by my ex lover because I denounced him for illicit
activities.”
[4]

She refused to participate to a formal hearing on same.

[
5
]

On March 3, 2009, Ms. Dakhova decided to file an
application for permanent residence which was dismissed.
[5]

[
6
]

In July 2009, Me Mankovitz, who was admitted to
the Quebec Bar in 2007, agreed to represent Ms. Dakhova before the Immigration
and Refugee Board (the “
Board
”)
[6]

and the Federal Court of Canada
[7]

where Ms. Dakhova accused Mr. Goikhberg and another person of inventing the
story with her ex lover to deceive immigration officials and the Board
[8]
.

[
7
]

On March 24, 2010
[9]
,
Mr. Goikhberg was arrested and charged with 20 counts of economic crimeS. He
remained in prison for the duration of the criminal proceedings and was
convicted on all charges in April 2011 and sentenced to five years of
imprisonment and a restitution order on September 9, 2011.
[10]

[
8
]

In the meantime, on April 26, 2010, the Board
dismissed Ms. Dakhova’s request for refugee status. Her appeal before the
Federal Court was also dismissed.

[
9
]

On September 26, 2011, Mr. Goikhberg appeared
before a judge to respond to 149 additional criminal counts
[11]
. The period of time covered
by the new charges is the same as the one for which Mr. Goikhberg was convicted
on April 20, 2011.
[12]

Mr. Goikhberg claims that Ms. Dakhova’s is amongst the persons who gave false
statements to the authorities which led to these additional charges.

[
10
]

In November 2014, Mr. Goikhberg called Me
Mankovitz. Following that conversation, he sent her a letter demanding $
500,000
[13]

detailed as follows:

a)

$ 15,000 in payment of the
“agreed
compensation for wrongdoing”
;

b)

$ 485,000 in punitive damages for influencing
different authorities against him for no reasonable justification.

[
11
]

Mr. Goikhberg claims that during their telephone
conversation of November 2014, Me Mankovitz admitted that she gave false
information to the authorities and agreed to pay him $ 15,000 by January 2015.
Mr. Goikhberg appealed to their common Jewish roots. After all, “
these
people”
[14]

exterminated people of the Jewish faith. Both his and Me Mankovitz’s
grandfather fought them together. Therefore, according to Mr. Goikhberg, Me
Mankovitz felt guilty for assisting Ms. Dakhova in making slanderous statements
against him and agreed to indemnify him. She would have told him that in 2009,
she was a young and inexperience lawyer. Therefore, according to Mr. Goikhberg,
she could not have realized yet how people from the ex-Soviet Union were ready
to say and do anything in order not to get deported.

[
12
]

Me Mankovitz’s version differs. She admits to
the telephone conversation but says that Mr. Goikhberg was distraught and
difficult to follow. He told her that he was getting out of jail and asked her
if she was a mother. She tried to make sense out of his various statements and
admits that she was empathetic, but denies having agreed to pay him anything.
In fact, at the time of the conversation, she thought that Mr. Goikhberg was
calling her about another client. It is only later that she realized that he
was speaking of Ms. Dakhova.

ANALYSIS

[
13
]

Mr. Goikhberg had to prove the facts on which
his claim is based
[15]
.
The evidence must be such that it renders the existence of the facts alleged by
him more probable than their non-existence
[16]
.
This probability is assessed using direct and circumstantial evidence,
inferences and presumptions
[17]
.

1)

Is there an agreement between Mr. Goikhberg
and Me Mankovitz for the payment of $ 15,000?

[
14
]

Article 2862 C.C.Q. reads as follows:

2862
. Proof of a juridical act may not be made, between
the parties, by testimony where the value in dispute exceeds $1,500.

However, in the absence of proof in
writing and regardless of the value in dispute, proof may be made by testimony
of any juridical act where there is a commencement of proof; proof may also be
made by testimony, against a person, of a juridical act executed by him in the
ordinary course of business of an enterprise.

[
15
]

Mr. Goikhberg has no written proof of the
alleged agreement, which would be a juridical act, for the payment of $15,000.

[
16
]

Mr. Goikhberg cannot benefit from the exception
provided in the second paragraph of article 2862 C.C.Q. Indeed, the alleged
agreement was not entered into in the ordinary course of business of either Mr.
Goikhberg or Me Mankovitz.

[
17
]

Furthermore, there is no commencement of proof
in writing of the alleged deal.

[
18
]

In any event, the Court has no difficulty to
accept Me Mankovitz’s version of the telephone conversation. It makes no sense
for a lawyer to agree to pay such a sum of money on a mere telephone
conversation. There was no previous contractual relationship between Mr.
Goikhberg and Me Mankovitz.

[
19
]

Mr. Goikhberg’s call came more than 5 years
after Me Mankovitz’s letter to the Board
[18]

and more than 4 years after the sworn statement of Ms. Dakhova to the Federal
Court
[19]
.
Rules of prescription are basic in the practice of law and Me Mankovitz was
perfectly aware of them.

[
20
]

Finally, Mr. Goikhberg’s claim could have been
dealt with by Me Mankovitz professional liability insurer. She had no advantage
to
“make a deal”
with Mr. Goikhberg.

[
21
]

Therefore, the Court has no hesitation to
conclude that there was no agreement between Mr. Goikhberg and Me Mankovitz for
the payment of $ 15,000.

2)

Can Me Mankovitz be condemned to pay damages to Mr.
Goikhberg for the statements made on behalf of Ms. Dakhova to the Board and the
Federal Court?

[
22
]

In the absence of a contractual obligation, the
Court has to decide if Me Mankovitz can be held to the payment of damages to
Mr. Goikhberg as a result of the statements contained in documents drafted to
assist Ms. Dakhova in her demand for refugee status.

[
23
]

The impugned statements were made in July 2009
[20]
and reiterated in a Court
proceedings dated September 2010.
[21]

By September 26, 2011, the relationship between Ms. Dakhova and Mr. Goikhberg
had resulted in criminal charges against Mr. Goikhberg. Mr. Goikhberg’s action
against Me Mankovitz was instituted on December 14, 2015.

[
24
]

Article 2925 C.C.Q. reads as follows:

2925
. An action to enforce a personal right or movable
real right is prescribed by three years, if the prescriptive period is not
otherwise determined.

[
25
]

Mr. Goikhberg’s action was instituted more than
three years after the alleged statements and more than three years after the
criminal charges resulting therefrom. Therefore, Mr. Goikhberg’s action is
prescribed.

[
26
]

Mr. Goikhberg claims that during his
imprisonment, it was impossible for him to act in order to institute legal
proceedings or appear in Court.
[22]

[
27
]

However, according to established jurisprudence,
incarceration in a Canadian prison does not constitute a cause of impossibility
in fact to act for purposes of prescription under the C.C.Q. in the absence of
specific circumstances that Mr. Goikhberg has failed to prove.
[23]

[
28
]

Mr. Goikhberg also claims that he found out
about Me Mankovitz’s involvement in Ms. Dakhova’s lies only shortly prior to
their phone call of November 2014, when he found a copy of the Board’s decision
amongst the documents obtained through the disclosure of the evidence in case
number 500-73-003628-118. This disclosure occurred more than three years prior
to the institution of the present action. The fact that Mr. Goikhberg did not
find the decision then is not the result of an impossibility to act.

[
29
]

Therefore, Mr. Goikhberg’s action for extracontractual
damages is prescribed and must be dismissed.

[
30
]

The Court adds that the action must also be
dismissed given the absence of evidence that Me Mankovitz committed a fault.
[24]

[
31
]

As the attorney for Ms. Dakhova, Me Mankovitz is
an officer of the court who participating in the administration of justice
[25]
. It is important and in the
interest of truth that parties who have resorted to a Court of law to obtain
justice, be free to set forth their allegations and claims before the proper
authority. Therefore, lawyers must be able to express themselves freely in
order to carry out their duty and defend their client’s interest. Their
immunity should only end where bad faith begins.
[26]

[
32
]

As expressed by Judge Chaput, in
Juneau c.
Taillefer
[27]
:

24
Quant à l'avocat, il ne sera pas responsable envers les tiers à raison de
l'action ou de la procédure, si «avec l'habileté convenable et tout le soin
d'un bon père de famille» (art. 1710 C.c.), il agit à l'intérieur des limites
de son mandat. Mais l'immunité offerte n'est pas absolue; elle tombe s'il y a
délit ou quasi-délit de l'avocat: allégation non pertinente susceptible de
causer un dommage, faite sans cause raisonnable et probable de croire à sa
véracité:

L'absence
de cause raisonnable et probable de croire à la vérité de l'allégation
injurieuse peut faire présumer et prouver la mauvaise foi et la malice; au
fond, dans des actions de ce genre, la mauvaise foi découlant de l'absence de
cause raisonnable et probable est le critère de la faute qui engage la
responsabilité de l'avocat.
13

dérogation
au

Code de déontologie des avocats
14
; manquement à soutenir l'administration de
la justice
15
; introduction d'une demande manifestement
vouée au rejet;

On
peut toutefois avancer, en guise de synthèse, qu'il y a recours abusif lorsque
le dossier constitué par les parties révèle l'inexistence d'un litige. Le
plaideur ou le plaignant fautif est généralement celui qui, ex nihilo, a
“fabriqué” un procès.
16

_________________

13.

Desmarchais c. Morin
, R.J., CS 1961, pp 465-475, à la p. 471.

14.

R.R.Q., 1981,
c. B-1, r. 1
.

15
.
Panorama Inc. c. Michel Gauthier et Chantale
Bilodeau
, C.A. Montréal,
500-09-000432-898
,  30 avril 1985
.

16.

Yves-Marie
Morissette

L'initiative
judiciaire

vouée à l'échec et la
responsabilité de l'avocat ou de son [texte illisible], 44 Revue du bareau
(1944), 397, 441.

[
33
]

Me Mankovitz did not act in bad faith and her
reliance on Ms. Dakhova’s account of her encounter with Mr. Goikhberg appears
to be reasonable given the outcome of Mr. Goikhberg legal contentions with the
authority as a result of same.

3
)
Is Mr. Goikhberg’s action abusive, frivolous or does it
reflects a conduct that is vexatious or quarrelsome?

[
34
]

Me Mankovitz asks for the dismissal of Mr.
Goikhberg’s action based on articles 51 and following of the
Code of civil
procedure
[28]

which read as follows:

51.
The courts may, at any time, on an
application and even on their own initiative, declare that a judicial
application or a pleading is abusive.

Regardless of intent, the abuse of procedure may
consist in a judicial application or pleading that is clearly unfounded,
frivolous or intended to delay or in conduct that is vexatious or quarrelsome.
It may also consist in a use of procedure that is excessive or unreasonable or
that causes prejudice to another person, or attempts to defeat the ends of
justice, particularly if it operates to restrict another person’s freedom of
expression in public debate.

52.

If a party
summarily establishes that a judicial application or pleading may constitute an
abuse of procedure, the onus is on the initiator of the application or pleading
to show that it is not excessive or unreasonable and is justified in law.

The
application is presented and defended orally, and decided by the court on the
face of the pleadings and exhibits in the record and the transcripts of any
pre-trial examinations. No other evidence is presented, unless the court
considers it necessary.

[…]

53.

If there has been
an abuse of procedure, the court may dismiss the judicial application or reject
a pleading, strike out a conclusion or require that it be amended, terminate or
refuse to allow an examination, or cancel a subpoena.

[
35
]

The decision of the Court is to dismiss Mr.
Goikhberg’s action for tardiness and absence of a legal basis. Therefore, it
suffices to state, at this stage, that Mr. Goikhberg’s action against Me
Mankovitz defeats the ends of justice as it is in retaliation for what he
considers an unfair criminal conviction in which Me Mankovitz played no role.

FOR THESE REASONS, THE COURT:

DISMISSES
Mr.
Yafim Goikhberg’s action.

CONDEMNS
Mr. Yafim Goikhberg to pay to
Me Deborah Mankovitz the court fees of $ 190.00.

________________________________

MARTINE
L. TREMBLAY, J.C.
Q.

Date of hearing: June 20, 2016.
